description: Our approach is built around creativity, critical thinking, and a passion to learn through experience.
summary:
We developed Plop Space, an interactive web application that transforms complex space mission logistics into accessible education for kids ages 7 to 18. Currently, space science is too often treated as an adult-only topic. Educational materials are usually abstract or overly technical, leaving young minds completely unable to understand real missions and causing childhood dreams to fade.

Super SUNic solves this by putting kids directly in the role of mission commanders on the Moon and Mars. To simulate genuine engineering trade-offs, players actively balance competing demands like life support, power, food production, and radiation shielding. Every single decision features clear pros and cons, teaching them that no choice in deep space is ever "free."

To maximize accessibility, the app features simple language, multi-language support, age-adaptive difficulty, narrated voice guides, and offline play. By turning passive screen time into an active learning experience, Supersonic bridges the gap between childhood curiosity and actual science, ensuring no kid's dream of space dies halfway.
details:
Overview and Purpose Plop Space is an interactive, educational space survival web application created by Team Globlu (Maryam Nizam and Bahja Hafeel). Designed to transform intimidating space science into a hands-on adventure for young minds, the application directly addresses a major educational gap: almost 0% of children learn about space weather, and less than 5% of schools even mention it. Built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and thoroughly tested across laptops, tablets, and smartphones, Plop Space turns passive screen time into active problem-solving to build daily space weather awareness and early STEM confidence.

Accessibility and Onboarding The game begins with a personalized onboarding experience that prioritizes accessibility and inclusivity. Players first select from 11 languages—placing Sinhala, Tamil, and English alongside global languages—and choose between two age brackets (7–12 or 12–18) to tailor mission difficulty. To ensure that even early readers can play independently, an interactive read-out-loud voice narrator powered by the Web Speech API introduces them to their Moon or Mars mission.

Gameplay and Life Support Management Once on the planetary surface, players step into the role of mission commanders managing six core life-support systems:

  • A solar panel station
  • Air and water purifiers
  • A space dirt (regolith) radiation shield
  • A solar storm safe house
  • Lunar cabbage and lettuce farms
  • A waste recycler

As commanders face escalating planetary challenges, every task presents three action choices complete with clear pros and cons. Each decision directly impacts the colony's food, water, energy, and waste levels, requiring thoughtful resource management.

Learning Reinforcement and Progression Between survival stages, interactive mini-quizzes reinforce key scientific concepts using simple, jargon-free language paired with bright visuals and sound effects. Completing these challenges earns players mission credits, which can be spent to upgrade colony systems and unlock advanced levels.

Real-World Data and Offline Resilience Grounded in authentic NASA lunar plant-growth research and connected to NASA’s live DONKI space weather API, Plop Space brings real-world science directly into gameplay. Crucially, the application is engineered for resilience in regions like Sri Lanka that experience frequent power cuts and unstable internet; it automatically caches live NASA data while online and seamlessly switches to an offline mode using saved data during blackouts.

Future Vision Following positive initial playtests, Team Globlu plans to pilot Plop Space directly in Sri Lankan classrooms. Future updates will expand the platform with collaborative multiplayer modes, new planetary environments, and a custom Rocket and Rover Builder.
